summary: Invoice fluctuation from queued postback reordering and quantization tariff mapping
description:
Issue summary:
Customer Lexicon Health reports two finalized invoices (2026-02 and 2026-03 draft) with a delta of ~$4,200 after our billing system applied a provisional negative reserve credit which was later reversed. The customer uses a mix of quantized model variants and experienced a region failover during a large batch run on 2026-02-28.

Impact:
- Customer saw an unexpected credit on their provisional invoice (negative line) which reduced the draft by ~4,200 USD and then the final invoice increased back after postback processing — they are requesting an explanation and a corrective adjustment or refund if appropriate.

Environment:
- Production, us-east-1 serving fleet. Dedicated enterprise account using reserved capacity with hosted fallback for overflow. Mixed-queue batch jobs with quantized model variants.

Steps to reproduce (customer run):
1) Start multi-model batch job integrating redwood-compat-1.0-q8 and gpt-style-open-ql-quantized on 2026-02-28 22:15 UTC.
2) Routing triggered hosted fallback to us-east-1-hosted during local dedicated GPU pool congestion.
3) Postbacks from ingest pipeline queued during fallback window and later replayed to billing service out of timestamp order after region failover.
4) Billing applied a provisional reserve credit tied to a temporary tariff mapping for quantized variants (q8 tariff), then a reordering correlation caused the provisional credit to be localized to a different hourly window and subsequently removed during reconciliation.

Observed behavior:
- Draft invoice (2026-02-28 provisional) showed a -$4,200 reserve adjustment line.
- Finalized invoice reverted the credit resulting in an unexpected $4,200 increase.
- Customer reports this is material to month-end accounting and expects clear audit trail.

Expected behavior:
- Postbacks should be ordered deterministically (or have a stable reconciliation policy) so provisional credits are not applied to the wrong hourly buckets; tariff mapping for quantized variants should be stable and reversible with clear audit logs.

Logs & evidence provided by customer:
- Customer attached a CSV of postback timestamps and job ids (submitted).
- Billing provisional vs finalized invoice PDF screenshots (submitted).
- Job manifest and routing logs (available in S3: s3://lexicon-health/2026-02-28/batch-manifest.json).

Customer requested outcome:
- Explanation for the sudden credit reversal and a request for either a pro-rated refund/credit or a waiver for the final invoice delta.
- A clear audit trail of which postbacks created and then removed the provisional credit and a plan to prevent recurrence.

investigation_notes:
- Pulled ingestion logs for window 2026-02-28T22:00 to 2026-03-01T06:00. Found 3 distinct requeue events on consumer instance consumer-7.
- Provisional credit originates from pricing-service rule "quantized-temp-reserve" which applies when model_variant tag missing but q8 heuristics match.
- Reconciliation job (hourly-reconciler v1.9.2) de-duplicates on postback_id and then re-evaluates tariff using model_version if present. Out-of-order replay causes temporary application of "quantized-temp-reserve" that is reversed when later message with model_version arrives.
- Related internal task INT-4421 opened to add ingestion-sequence-id and to make temporary-tariff non-destructive (i.e., mark provisional but don't finalize until reconciliation window closes).
- Calculated affected usage bucket: 18:00-19:00 UTC on 2026-02-28 had ~312k tokens attributed under q8 provisional; reversal re-attributed ~295k tokens at standard hosted tariff producing delta ~4200 USD.
- Evidence artifacts uploaded to internal bucket: s3://redwood-internal/forensics/SUP-382991/.
resolution_notes:
Work in progress. Temporary mitigations: 1) Issued a provisional customer-facing statement acknowledging the discrepancy and promising priority reconciliation by 2026-03-15. 2) Billing team toggled the provisional rollback guard to delay automatic reversal for tickets flagged as high-touch. 3) Engineering to deploy ingestion-sequence-id patch in canary 2026-03-13 and a reconciliation policy change to mark provisional credits with lifecycle metadata.
Next steps: - Complete ingestion fix (INT-4421), re-run reconciliation for Lexicon Health account, and generate audit report showing which postback_ids caused apply/remove of the provisional credit. - If reconciliation confirms misapplied reversal, offer credit for the delta or a one-time billing waiver per CS escalation policy. - Follow-up with customer with final outcome and postmortem.
customer_requested_resolution: Customer asked for either a corrective credit of ~$4,200 on the next invoice or a one-time waiver and an audit CSV showing postback_id -> tariff decisions. They requested timeline: resolution by 2026-03-15.
outcome_options: Apply one-time credit of $4,200 after manual reconciliation
Issue waiver and upgraded billing SLA for one month
Decline adjustment if reconciliation shows correct final attribution (with full audit)
notes_for_finance: If manual credit is approved, finance to create credit memo referencing SUP-382991 and adjust account ledger before 2026-03-20. Include line: 'Provisional postback reordering adjustment'.
